verdicts.evidence: Checked raw sources on 2026-10-08/09. pinctrl-bcm2835.c, both rpi-6.12.y and rpi-6.18.y, lines 248-250: 'static bool persist_gpio_outputs = true; module_param(persist_gpio_outputs, bool, 0444); ... "Enable GPIO_OUT persistence when pin is freed"'. bcm2835_pmx_free (6.18 line 965ff): 'if (persist_gpio_outputs && fsel == BCM2835_FSEL_GPIO_OUT) return 0;'. Only otherwise does it set GPIO_IN. pinctrl-rp1.c, both branches, line 578: 'static bool persist_gpio_outputs = true;' with module_param mode 0644. rp1_pmx_free (6.18 line 1265ff): 'if (persist_gpio_outputs && fsel == RP1_FSEL_GPIO) return 0;'. Release path in rpi-6.18.y: gpiolib-cdev frees each line with gpiod_free() (lines 279/1579/1923). gpiod_free_commit (gpiolib.c 2550ff) calls gc->free, which is gpiochip_generic_free on both chips (bcm2835 line 395, rp1 line 791). That reaches the pinmux .gpio_disable_free, which calls bcm2835_pmx_free / rp1_pmx_free. gpiod_free_commit itself clears only software flags and does not touch direction or value, so a pin set to output keeps its function and level once its file descriptors close, including on SIGKILL. The bcm2835 driver logs 'GPIO_OUT persistence: yes|no' at probe (line 1476), so dmesg on the target shows the active setting. Details: on RP1 the persistence check is on the GPIO function regardless of direction. The RP1 parameter is 0644, so it can be changed at runtime; the bcm2835 one is 0444, boot-time only.

Downloaded the PDF from https://pip-assets.raspberrypi.com/categories/685-whitepapers-app-notes/documents/RP-006553-WP/A-history-of-GPIO-usage-on-Raspberry-Pi-devices-and-current-best-practices (14 pages). Release table: '1 / 1 Aug 2024 / Initial release; 2 / 13 Aug 2025 / Update to Wiring Pi section'. Verbatim text: 'In order to make the move from the persistent operations of the previous sysfs to libgpiod easier, the Raspberry Pi kernel modifies this behaviour so that the state of a GPIO IS retained when a program that has changed the value (e.g. gpioset, see below) exits. You can enable the automatic reversion behaviour of libgpiod by adding the following to the config.txt file. dtparam=strict_gpiod'. It continues: 'Alternatively, add the following to the kernel command line (cmdline.txt). pinctrl_bcm2835.persist_gpio_outputs=n'. Caveat: that cmdline alternative names only the bcm2835 driver. On a Pi 5 the parameter is pinctrl_rp1.persist_gpio_outputs=n (see C30).

rpi-6.18.y arch/arm/boot/dts/broadcom/bcm270x-rpi.dtsi line 121: 'strict_gpiod = <&chosen>, "bootargs=pinctrl_bcm2835.persist_gpio_outputs=n";'. arch/arm64/boot/dts/broadcom/bcm2712-rpi.dtsi line 245: 'strict_gpiod = <&chosen>, "bootargs=pinctrl_rp1.persist_gpio_outputs=n";'. The override appends rather than replaces the existing bootargs (which contain cgroup_disable=memory etc.). Raspberry Pi's dtoverlay implementation special-cases bootargs: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raspberrypi/utils/master/dtmerge/dtoverlay.c lines 1755-1761, '/* Append to or replace the property string */ if ((strcmp(prop_name, "bootargs") == 0) && ... ) fdt_appendprop(...)'. Overlays README (rpi-6.18.y, line 449): 'strict_gpiod  Return GPIOs to inputs when they are released. If using the gpiod utilities, it is necessary to keep a gpioset running (e.g. with --mode=wait) in order for an output value to persist.' The parameter is enforced in the pinctrl driver on line release, so it applies to any process that holds lines through /dev/gpiochipN, in or out of a container (lgpio does). Scope limits: it acts only on lines requested through the GPIO character device. Pins written directly through /dev/gpiomem (RPi.GPIO, pigpio, pinctrl) are never 'released' and keep their state. It also does nothing while the holding process is alive but hung.

verdicts.corrected_claim: strict_gpiod is not automatically safe for active-low relays. On release, bcm2835_pmx_free only sets the function to GPIO_IN, and rp1_pmx_free only sets the input direction and GPIO function. Neither touches the pull/bias, so the pin keeps whatever bias was last configured, not necessarily the power-on default. With the accepted gpiozero + lgpio stack that bias is 'disabled'. LGPIOPin.__init__ first claims every pin as input with lgpio.SET_PULL_NONE (= GPIO_V2_LINE_FLAG_BIAS_DISABLED). The later output claim passes no bias flags, which means 'as-is'. So after a crash with strict_gpiod, BCM 22/23 are floating inputs, not inputs with the ~50 kΩ pull-down. The same holds after a normal gpiozero close, which re-claims each pin as input with SET_PULL_NONE. The released state therefore differs from the boot state. At boot the pins are inputs with the default pull-down: documented for BCM2835/2711 (GPIO 9-27 pull low). For the Pi 5 it rests only on a Raspberry Pi engineer's forum statement, because the RP1 datasheet lists the reset pulls as 'varies'. Whether the active-low relay board stays off with a floating or weakly pulled input is board-dependent and must be measured. A HAL that requests the output lines with an explicit pull-up bias (allowed by the GPIO v2 uAPI) would make the released state deterministic, because the pull survives release.
verdicts.evidence: Release functions: pinctrl-bcm2835.c and pinctrl-rp1.c rpi-6.18.y, bcm2835_pmx_free and rp1_pmx_free (see C28). Neither touches pull/bias. gpiozero master gpiozero/pins/lgpio.py lines 127-128 (__init__): 'lgpio.gpio_claim_input(self.factory._handle, self._number, lgpio.SET_PULL_NONE)'. Lines 130-135 (close): '# Closing is really just "resetting" the function of the pin ... lgpio.gpio_claim_input(..., lgpio.SET_PULL_NONE)'. _set_function calls lgpio.gpio_claim_output(handle, number) with no flags. joan2937/lg lgGpio.c line 239: 'if (s & LG_SET_PULL_NONE) f |= GPIO_V2_LINE_FLAG_BIAS_DISABLED;'. Both drivers apply BIAS_DISABLE in hardware (bcm2835 set_config = gpiochip_generic_config, PIN_CONFIG_BIAS_DISABLE handled at lines 1122/1166/1235; rp1 line 1395/1502). gpiolib-cdev.c rpi-6.18.y lines 1192-1195: '/* Bias requires explicit direction. */', so bias together with OUTPUT is accepted in uAPI v2. Pi 5 pulls: https://forums.raspberrypi.com/viewtopic.php?t=366826 PhilE 2024-03-04: 'As with BCM2835 et al, 0-8 default to pull-ups, 9-27 pull down'. In the same thread, jdb notes that RP1 Table 21 lists the PUE/PDE defaults as 'varies'.

verdicts.corrected_claim: Docker restart policies have no post-stop hook. Docker's docs say 'Docker recommends that you use restart policies, and avoid using process managers to start containers' and warn 'Don't combine Docker restart policies with host-level process managers, as this creates conflicts.' A systemd unit wrapping a foreground (attached, no -d, no --restart) `docker run` does notice container death: the client exits with the container's exit code, so ExecStopPost runs after a container crash, OOM kill or kill -9. What systemd cannot do is see or control the container processes themselves. They run under containerd-shim (not as children of dockerd), outside the unit's cgroup. If the client is killed, loses its connection, or dockerd/containerd restarts, the unit's state and ExecStopPost diverge from the container's real state. It is therefore a fragile, Docker-discouraged pattern, not an impossible one.
verdicts.evidence: https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/start-containers-automatically/: 'Docker recommends that you use restart policies, and avoid using process managers to start containers.'; 'Don't combine Docker restart policies with host-level process managers, as this creates conflicts.' The page mentions no hooks or post-stop actions. https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/run/ (Exit status): 'The exit code from docker run gives information about why the container failed to run or why it exited.' Codes other than 125/126/127 are the container command's own exit status, so the attached client returns when the container exits. https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/: --sig-proxy defaults to true ('Proxy received signals to the process'). The claim's statements are true as worded. The implied conclusion (ExecStopPost cannot work with Docker) and the phrase 'child of the daemon' are imprecise.

verdicts.corrected_claim: PID 1 in a container receives a signal only if it has installed a handler for it. The exception is SIGKILL/SIGSTOP sent from an ancestor namespace, which are forcibly delivered, so docker stop's final SIGKILL always lands. CPython installs no SIGTERM handler by default: it ignores SIGPIPE (and SIGXFSZ) and maps SIGINT to KeyboardInterrupt. If PID 1 is a shell wrapper that does not exec the app, or an app without a SIGTERM handler, docker/podman stop ends in SIGKILL after the 10 s timeout, and with C28 the outputs stay as they were. uvicorn installs SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers only when serving in the main thread. Exec-form ENTRYPOINT or --init fixes signal delivery but does not by itself turn the outputs off. With --init, tini forwards SIGTERM to a non-PID-1 Python, and without a handler Python dies immediately on the default action. Since uvicorn 0.29.0 ('Cooperative signal handling', #1600), Server.capture_signals also restores the previous handlers after graceful shutdown and re-raises the captured signal (signal.raise_signal). Whenever Python is not PID 1 (native systemd, --init, Quadlet RunInit=) and the previous handler is SIG_DFL, the process is terminated right there. Code placed after server.serve()/uvicorn.run() returns never runs. The HW-021 'all outputs off' step must therefore run inside the Starlette lifespan shutdown, or in an app-installed handler/finally that executes before uvicorn's re-raise.
verdicts.evidence: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/pid_namespaces.7.html: 'Only signals for which the "init" process has established a signal handler can be sent to the "init" process by other members of the PID namespace ... SIGKILL or SIGSTOP are treated exceptionally: these signals are forcibly delivered when sent from an ancestor PID namespace.' https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/container/run/: 'A process running as PID 1 inside a container is treated specially by Linux: it ignores any signal with the default action.' This note is in the --attach section; the --init section only says an init process is used as PID 1. --stop-timeout default '10 seconds for Linux containers'. CPython Modules/signalmodule.c lines 1936-1944: PyOS_setsig(SIGPIPE/SIGXFZ/SIGXFSZ, SIG_IGN). Python docs say SIGPIPE ignored and SIGINT to KeyboardInterrupt. uvicorn master server.py lines 45-48: HANDLED_SIGNALS = (SIGINT, SIGTERM). Lines 329-346 (capture_signals): 'if threading.current_thread() is not threading.main_thread(): yield; return' ... restores original handlers ... 'for captured_signal in reversed(self._captured_signals): signal.raise_signal(captured_signal)'. uvicorn docs/release-notes.md: '## 0.29.0 (March 19, 2024) ... Cooperative signal handling (#1600)'.

Multiple ExecStopPost= lines are allowed by systemd, so a user GPIO-reset ExecStopPost coexists with Quadlet's own cleanup commands.

missed: Hang vs crash: every NFR-003 mechanism examined here acts only when the GPIO-holding process dies and its file descriptors close: ExecStopPost, strict_gpiod, and kernel release on SIGKILL. A hung app (blocked event loop) with the heater ON keeps the line requested and the heater on indefinitely. That needs a liveness watchdog. Natively: systemd WatchdogSec= with sd_notify WATCHDOG=1; on timeout systemd kills the service, ExecStopPost runs and Restart= applies. Podman Quadlet: HealthOnFailure=kill plus Restart= (man page: 'Once the container turns unhealthy, it gets killed, and systemd restarts the service'). Docker: restart policies react only to container exit, not to health status (open feature requests https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/28400 and https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/49161; their current state was not re-checked). This needs an extra component such as willfarrell/docker-autoheal, which requires the Docker socket. This favours native or Quadlet over Docker.

gpiozero + lgpio never leaves the relay pins driven HIGH after the process ends, even on a clean stop. LGPIOPin.close() re-claims each pin as input with SET_PULL_NONE (bias disabled), and the factory then frees the lines (gpiozero/pins/lgpio.py lines 130-135). After a normal SIGTERM shutdown the active-low relay inputs are therefore floating. That is the same state as after a strict_gpiod crash release, and different from the boot state (pull-down). The hardware relay test must cover the floating case. A host-side ExecStopPost that re-drives the pins (e.g. `pinctrl set 22,23 op dh`, direct register writes with no line request, so unaffected by strict_gpiod) makes the post-stop state deterministic. Alternatively, a HAL that requests the outputs with an explicit pull-up bias leaves a pull-up behind on release.

Combining strict_gpiod with a host-side reset helper based on libgpiod is self-defeating. The overlays README says that with strict_gpiod 'it is necessary to keep a gpioset running ... in order for an output value to persist'. A gpioset/libgpiod ExecStopPost that exits would see its HIGH reverted to input. Use pinctrl (register writes, no line request), or accept the input state.

On the Pi 5 the persistence switch is writable at runtime. pinctrl-rp1 declares module_param(persist_gpio_outputs, bool, 0644), so root can write N to /sys/module/pinctrl_rp1/parameters/persist_gpio_outputs. On Pi 3/4 the pinctrl-bcm2835 parameter is 0444 and needs the boot parameter (dtparam=strict_gpiod). The whitepaper's cmdline.txt alternative names only pinctrl_bcm2835.persist_gpio_outputs=n, which has no effect on a Pi 5 (that needs pinctrl_rp1.persist_gpio_outputs=n). Prefer dtparam=strict_gpiod, which picks the right driver per board, and verify with dmesg ('GPIO_OUT persistence: no', printed by pinctrl-bcm2835) or the sysfs parameter.

uvicorn >= 0.29.0 re-raises the captured SIGTERM after restoring the previous handler (server.py capture_signals). In native systemd, under --init, or with Quadlet RunInit=, this terminates the process before any code after uvicorn.run()/server.serve() runs. The HW-021 outputs-off step must live in the Starlette lifespan shutdown, or the app must install its own SIGTERM handler before uvicorn so that handler is what gets restored. This applies to every deployment mode, not just containers.

The Pi 5 default pull-down on BCM 22/23 is not documented in the RP1 datasheet (Table 21 lists the PUE/PDE defaults as 'varies'). It rests on a single Raspberry Pi engineer's forum post (2024-03-04), so the boot-time relay state on a Pi 5 should be measured too.
